slot.brief: Circuit with ideal diodes in series/parallel with resistors; determine which diodes conduct and compute the current through a specified branch.

stem: In the circuit shown in the figure, both diodes are ideal. What is the current through diode $D_1$?

verdicts.working: The two 4 Ω branches are in parallel, giving 2 Ω. Total resistance is 2 Ω + 2 Ω = 4 Ω, so the source current is 12/4 = 3 A. Equal branches carry 1.5 A each; therefore the current through D₁ is 1.5 A.

working:
$R_{\text{parallel}} = 4\parallel 4 = 2\ \Omega$
$R_{\text{total}} = 2 + 2 = 4\ \Omega$
$I_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3\ \text{A}$
$D_1,D_2$ both conduct; equal branch resistances give $I_{D_1} = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5\ \text{A}$

Independent check: The two 4 Ω branches are in parallel, giving 2 Ω. Total resistance is 2 Ω + 2 Ω = 4 Ω, so the source current is 12/4 = 3 A. Equal branches carry 1.5 A each; therefore the current through D₁ is 1.5 A.

draft.stem: In the circuit shown in the figure, both diodes are ideal. What is the current through diode $D_1$?

figure.description: Draw a 12 V ideal battery on the left, with its positive terminal above its negative terminal. Connect the positive terminal through a 2 Ω resistor to an upper junction. From this junction draw two parallel vertical branches to a common lower junction. In the left branch, place a 4 Ω resistor above an ideal diode labelled D1; in the right branch, place a 4 Ω resistor above an ideal diode labelled D2. Orient both diodes to conduct downward (anode above cathode). Connect the lower junction to the battery's negative terminal. Label all component values and the battery polarity.

draft.distractor_notes: A: halves the branch current again. B: incorrect current division. D: gives the total current rather than the current in one branch.
